readings: In `Products`, find each `production_type_code`'s average `unit_price` (ignoring missing prices) and keep the types whose average is above the overall average price, if that average exists. Next, take the simple mean of the kept types' averages, and keep only the types also above that mean. Return one row with three values, each averaged over the remaining types: their type average price, how far their type average is above the overall average price, and how far it is above the mean of the kept types.
queries:
WITH type_avg AS (
  SELECT production_type_code, AVG(unit_price) AS avg_price
  FROM Products
  GROUP BY production_type_code
  HAVING AVG(unit_price) IS NOT NULL
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(unit_price) AS overall_avg FROM Products
),
kept1 AS (
  SELECT t.production_type_code, t.avg_price
  FROM type_avg t, overall o
  WHERE t.avg_price > o.overall_avg
),
mean_kept AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_price) AS m FROM kept1
),
kept2 AS (
  SELECT k.production_type_code, k.avg_price
  FROM kept1 k, mean_kept mk
  WHERE k.avg_price > mk.m
)
SELECT AVG(k.avg_price) AS avg_type_price,
       AVG(k.avg_price - o.overall_avg) AS above_overall,
       AVG(k.avg_price - mk.m) AS above_kept_mean
FROM kept2 k, overall o, mean_kept mk;
